extracted.intended_audience: NLP/AI researchers and practitioners working on patent analysis, textual entailment, and automated patent examination support
extracted.subtask_description: Framing the task of deciding patent claim novelty (and predicting claim edits) as a textual entailment problem: given prior art citations and draft claim sentences, predict which sentences/claims are novel or must be revised. The paper introduces a 105K-example dataset of successful claim revisions and evaluates LLMs on sentence-level edit prediction using entailment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent must be deemed novel and non-obvious in order to be granted by the US Patent Office (USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim is not novel, a US patent examiner will cite the prior work, or prior art, that invalidates the novelty and issue a non-final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art citation as examiner mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners cite prior art that invalidates the novelty of claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations of prior art are used to justify non-final rejections; successful prosecution requires addressing those citations (e.g., via claim amendments or arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful claim revisions overcome novelty objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to patent drafts (claims/specification) that overcome examiner objections to novelty constitute successful edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PatentEdits dataset contains 105K examples of successful revisions that overcome objections to novelty — these examples serve as targets for learnable models that predict what claims should change given prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level labeling of edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits can be labeled sentence by sentence to indicate which sentences were changed and which remained, helping identify the parts of claims that were novel or required modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors design algorithms to label edits at the sentence level, enabling models to learn from fine-grained supervision about how claim language evolves in response to prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual entailment between cited references and draft sentences as a predictor of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating textual entailment between cited references (prior art) and draft claim sentences is an effective method for predicting which inventive claims remained unchanged or are novel relative to prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper demonstrates that framing patent novelty as a textual entailment problem improves prediction of which edits succeed; thus entailment-related metrics or model outputs can be used as evaluation signals for claim novelty and edit necessity.
